messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Streaming tail/p99 latency breach detected for /v1/stream endpoints in us-west-2. p99 spiked to ~12s, p95 ~1.8s over last 5m. Auto-escalating to oncall (alex).

alex (oncall): On it. seeing ALOT of stalled chunking in the proxy-frontend logs. marking priority-high and starting triage.

sara (infra): Confirmed. Proxy write latency and connection buffer growth. Nginx upstream queuing counts increased. Could be a sudden slow consumer surge from a few clients.

mike (runtime): Any recent deploys to streaming runtime or proxy config in the last hour?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: New config rollback disabled flag flipped at 3081232000 by infra-rollout (sara). No streaming runtime deploys in the last 3h.

jin (support): Customer chatter: two enterprise customers reported intermittent stalls in live chat. They see long pauses between chunks.

alex (oncall): OK. start with quick mitigations: 1) throttle high-conn clients, 2) bump proxy worker count, 3) toggle chunk-flush to aggressive. Sara, can infra scale proxy pool now?

sara (infra): Scaling + adding 4 proxy instances in us-west-2. Doing a rolling restart of frontline proxies with increased `sendfile` timeouts.

sara (infra): Also increasing `proxy_buffer_size` and `proxy_busy_buffers_size`. Will monitor.

mike (runtime): I'm enabling more aggressive KV/prefix caching eviction to reduce backend token generation stalls (temporary).

alex (oncall): Throttle rule applied to suspicious IPs via WAF: limit 4 concurrent streams per token.

jin (support): Notifying affected customers that we're investigating and applying mitigations. Template used: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls; temporary throttling may be applied."

tori (sre): Seeing immediate drop in queue length on restarted proxies, p95 trending down. p99 still has a long tail for some sessions.

mike (runtime): I pulled a tail of logs from a stuck session:
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:30Z] connection id=abcd write failed: EPIPE after 9s
[2026-03-15T14:12:30Z] runtime: out-of-session backpressure, waiting for client ACK
[2026-03-15T14:12:31Z] proxy: upstream chunk flush delayed by 7s
```
Looks like client-side backpressure + proxy buffer accumulation.

alex (oncall): Could be slow consumers holding connections and preventing proxies from freeing sockets. If proxies hit max open fd, others stall. Check `accept` queue and fd usage.

sara (infra): Checking nodes: fd usage peaked at 86%, accept queue growing. Increasing `ulimit -n` and spinning new proxy nodes done.

ops-bot: metric-alert: proxy_fd_utilization_us-west-2 crossed 80% at 3081234500.

mike (runtime): Two additional mitigations: 1) enable periodic flush of partial chunks every 200ms, 2) reduce internal batching to keep tail tokens flowing. Applying now as a runtime toggle.

alex (oncall): Applying chunk flush toggle. Monitor for increased token count and CPU.

sara (infra): Nginx config snippet pushed to canary proxies (us-west-2-canary):
```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_max_temp_file_size 0;
proxy_send_timeout 15s;
proxy_read_timeout 60s;
```

mike (runtime): After chunk flush + reduced batching, p95 200ms, p99 down to ~2.4s on canary. Good sign.

jin (support): Customers on the affected lists are seeing improved flow on the canary but a handful still report occasional pauses.

alex (oncall): Can we identify top 10 tokens/sessions causing tail? Dumped sessions show a handful of very chatty sessions holding connections open with low ACK rate. Suggest temporary per-token concurrent-stream cap to protect fleet.

sara (infra): WAF rule expanded to global: cap 3 concurrent streams / token for 10m. Also added time-windowed rate limits for new sessions from same IP.

ops-bot: action-log: applied global stream cap at 3081234588 by sara.

mike (runtime): Confirmed fewer stalls, p99 now ~1.1s cluster-wide. CPU bump expected but acceptable.

alex (oncall): Good. Start handoff checklist: Note mitigations taken, customer impact, and next steps. Tori, please pick this up for post-incident follow-up.

tori (sre): On it. I'll collect traces, top offending sessions, and link relevant dashboards. We should run a targeted test simulating slow consumer clients to reproduce.

jin (support): Customer impact summary to include: ~2.3% of streaming requests experienced >3s tail during the 14:08-14:58 window. Two enterprise customers opened support tickets, both received interim notifications.

alex (oncall): Logging a short incident page: will put current mitigations and the times applied.

mike (runtime): Notes for postmortem: investigate batching heuristics that allow single slow consumers to block shared buffers; consider per-connection write buffers and aggressive per-conn timeouts. Also add more conservative defaults for `proxy_buffering` for streaming endpoints.

sara (infra): Ops followup: add automated scaling on fd_utilization and a fine-grained metric for per-proxy accept queue. Also validate `ulimit` changes across instance types.

tori (sre): Next actions: 1) reproduce in staging with slow-consumer tool, 2) add synthetic p99 streaming test in k8s e2e, 3) draft postmortem and assign owners.

jin (support): I'll follow up with customers who reported issues with a timeline and the mitigations we applied.

alex (oncall): Handoff complete. Setting incident status -> watching, and assigning to tori for follow-up. If anything regresses ping me directly. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged. Handoff recorded. Severity: SEV3 -> watching.

tori (sre): Thanks team. Adding the incident to the triage board and setting a follow-up meeting. Closing thread here; will update the incident doc with final impact numbers and root-cause hypothesis.
